chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Riab, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And there is no blame upon you for what you mutually agreed upon after the obligation'.

He said: 'What you agree upon after the marriage contract is valid, and what was before the marriage contract is not valid except with her consent and by giving her something with which she is pleased'.

key_terms.الْفَرِيضَة: The obligation (referring to the initial mahr/dowry)

ai.seo_question: What is the validity of financial agreements made between spouses before and after the marriage contract in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the application of Quran 4:24, distinguishing between post-contractual mutual agreements (which are automatically valid) and pre-contractual stipulations (which require explicit female consent and consideration). It underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that a woman's financial rights in marriage are flexible and subject to her voluntary satisfaction, reinforcing the contractual nature of the mahr.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, form Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said,
‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [4:24] and there is no blame on you about what you mutually agree

from after the marriage, so it is allowed, and whatever was from before the marriage, so it is not allowed except by her agreement, and by something being given to her, so she would be pleased with it’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from ibn Mahbub from ibn Ri’ab from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “This is concerning my question before abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the words of Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, 4 . . .

it is not harmful for you if you agree upon it after marriage.’ [4:24] He (the Imam) said, ‘Whatever they agree upon after marriage is permissible and whatever is before marriage is not permissible except with her agreement and with something given to her to make her agree.’”
